subtitle: When the Valley Emptied and Memory Fought On

panels.shot: wide aerial view over a mist-veiled, abandoned Kangla fort and deserted paddy fields, with a lone Meitei rider in the foreground
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba sits on a weary pony at the edge of an empty Manipur valley, looking towards the silent Kangla citadel under a pale dawn sky.

dialogue.text: In 1819, the Meitei valley fell silent. This is Chahi Taret Khuntakpa—the Seven Years Devastation—when a kingdom emptied but a people refused to die in memory.

i18n.hi: १८१९ में मैतेइ घाटी थम गई। यही है चाही तरेत खुंतक्पा—सात साल की तबाही—जब राज्य उजड़ गया, पर यादों ने मरने से इंकार किया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from above onto Kangla fort bustling in earlier times, contrasting with the later silence
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba, younger and strong, walks through a lively Kangla courtyard filled with courtiers, soldiers, and priests, all under the shadow of the palace walls.

dialogue.text: Only years before, Kangla was alive. Kings of Manipur held court, rituals burned bright, and the valley’s rice-fields fed a proud kingdom.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही बरस पहले, कंगला धड़कता था। मणिपुर के राजा दरबार लगाते, अनुष्ठान चमकते, धान के खेतों से गौरवशाली राज्य पलता।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in the dim palace hall with tense, shadowed figures
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba stands at the edge of a royal council, watching rival Meitei princes argue before a weary king in the lamplight.

dialogue.text: But behind the drums of ritual came whispers of succession. Princes quarrelled over Kangla’s throne, each seeking allies beyond the misty hills.

i18n.hi: पर नगाड़ों के पीछे उतराधिकार की सरगोशियाँ थीं। राजकुमार कंगला की गद्दी पर झगड़ते, धुंधले पहाड़ों के पार नए सहारे खोजते।

panels.shot: dramatic side shot of a Meitei envoy before a distant Burmese palace, with Ava’s skyline in the haze
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba, now as a representative figure, stands in a hall in Ava, watching a Meitei prince bow deeply before a Burmese noble seated on a raised platform.

dialogue.text: More than once, Meitei princes rode to Ava and asked the Burmese kings for troops. Politics opened the door that later swallowed the valley.

i18n.hi: कई बार मैतेइ राजकुमार अवा तक घोड़े दौड़ाए, बर्मी राजाओं से फ़ौज माँगी। यही सियासत वो दरवाज़ा बनी जिसने घाटी को निगल लिया।

panels.shot: wide low-angle of a Burmese host on the march over the eastern ridges towards Manipur
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba stands on a ridge, gripping a spear, watching long lines of Burmese soldiers and porters snake along the mountain path toward the Manipur valley.

dialogue.text: In 1819, under Bodawpaya’s successors, the Burmese army marched west again. This time, the march did not end with a quick kingmaking.

i18n.hi: १८१९ में बोडावपाया के उत्तराधिकारियों ने फिर फ़ौज पश्चिम भेजी। इस बार कूच किसी जल्दी गद्दी-बदल से नहीं थमा।

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of the Manipur plain as the Burmese army descends, smoke rising in the distance
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba runs through a village lane as Burmese soldiers arrive, villagers fleeing in all directions, cattle scattering and houses burning in the background.

dialogue.text: Meitei chronicles and later scholars describe the invasion as a devastation. The Burmese forces overran the valley, broke resistance, and made occupation their aim.

i18n.hi: मैतेइ ग्रंथ और बाद के विद्वान इस हमले को महातबाही कहते हैं। बर्मी फ़ौजों ने घाटी रौंद दी, प्रतिरोध तोड़ा, और कब्ज़े को ही मक़सद बनाया।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of villagers bound together and marched, with Ava’s direction indicated by distant hills
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba, hands tied, walks in a long column of deportees—men, women and children—herded by Burmese soldiers along a muddy road out of the valley.

dialogue.text: Parratt and Tarapot recount mass deportations. Sources speak of tens of thousands marched east to Ava—leaving behind fields, shrines and the bones of ancestors.

i18n.hi: पैराट और तारापोट बड़े पैमाने पर निर्वासन का ज़िक्र करते हैं। स्रोत बताते हैं—दसियों हज़ार लोग अवा की ओर हाँके गए, पीछे खेत, देवालय और पुरखों की हड्डियाँ छोड़कर।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Khuman Ngamba glancing back at the receding valley through tears, the line of captives stretching ahead
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba turns his head for one last look at the distant Manipur hills, his face torn between fear and stubborn resolve as the column trudges on.

dialogue.speaker: Khuman Ngamba
dialogue.text: If my body goes to Ava, let my heart stay in Kangla.

i18n.hi: मेरा जिस्म अवा जाए तो जाए, दिल कंगला में ही रहेगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of the abandoned Manipur valley, with overgrown paddy and empty homesteads under grey clouds
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba stands alone in the middle of a deserted field, surrounded by collapsed huts and weed-choked paddies stretching to the horizon.

dialogue.text: Later accounts estimate that only a few thousand remained in the valley. A land once crowded with life was left to silence, hunger and slow, creeping grass.

i18n.hi: कहा जाता है, घाटी में बस कुछ हज़ार ही बचे। जो धरती कभी जनों से भरी थी, वहाँ अब सन्नाटा, भूख और रेंगती घास रह गई।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a thatched hut in the hills, lit by a small fire, with exiles huddled together
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba sits among Meitei refugees in a Cachar or hill village, sharing a bowl of rice with others as elders whisper stories in the flickering light.

dialogue.text: Many fled to Cachar, to the Naga and Kuki hills, to Assam. In strange lands they clung to words—names of rivers, gods, kings—to keep Manipur alive in memory.

i18n.hi: कई लोग कछार, नागा-कूकी पहाड़, असम की ओर भागे। अनजानी ज़मीनों में उन्होंने शब्दों को थामा—नदियों, देवताओं, राजाओं के नाम—ताकि याद में मणिपुर जिंदा रहे।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Ava plain with horsemen drilling, banners fluttering, and a distant palace skyline
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba, now in Burmese attire but still wearing a Meitei amulet, rides among a troop of horsemen training on the plains near Ava.

dialogue.text: In Ava, deported Manipuris became known as Cassay. Thant Myint-U notes them as skilled cavalrymen in Burmese service—warriors from a lost valley, now woven into another king’s army.

i18n.hi: अवा में निर्वासित मणिपुरी ‘कस्से’ कहलाए। थांत मिंट-यू उन्हें बर्मी सेना के निपुण घुड़सवार मानते हैं—खोई घाटी के योद्धा, अब दूसरे राजा की फ़ौज में बुने गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Khuman Ngamba seated at night by a campfire outside Ava, staring at a small Kangla token
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba crouches by a campfire, holding a tiny carved wooden Kangla gate, the bustle of the military camp fading into the darkness around him.

dialogue.speaker: Khuman Ngamba
dialogue.text: They can command my horse, not my dreams.

i18n.hi: वे घोड़े पर हुक्म चला सकते हैं, मेरे सपनों पर नहीं।

panels.shot: wide forest shot of Meitei exiles and Cachari allies listening to a messenger in a clearing
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba stands among armed exiles in a forest clearing, leaning forward as a dusty messenger delivers urgent news.

dialogue.text: Far from Ava, in the forests of Cachar, Meitei princes in exile plotted return. Rumours rode with the rains—of British moves against Burma, of new chances to reclaim Kangla.

i18n.hi: अवा से दूर, कछार के जंगलों में, जला-वतनी मैतेइ राजकुमार वापसी की साज़िशें बुनते। बारिश के साथ खबरें उड़तीं—बर्मा पर चढ़ाई की, ब्रिटिश हलचलों की, और कंगला छीनने के नए मौकों की।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Khuman Ngamba tightening a sword belt, with a British officer and Meitei prince in the blurred background
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba straps on his sword while, behind him, a Meitei prince speaks with a British officer over a rough campaign map spread on a tree stump.

dialogue.text: As the First Anglo-Burmese War unfolded, exiled Manipuris aligned with British campaigns. Politics had once invited Ava; now, new politics promised a path home.

i18n.hi: पहले अंग्रेज़-बर्मी युद्ध के बीच, जला-वतनी मणिपुरी ब्रिटिश मुहिमों से जुड़ गए। कभी जिसने अवा को बुलाया था, वही राजनीति अब घर वापसी की राह बनने लगी।

panels.shot: epic low-angle of Meitei-led forces advancing towards Manipur valley, hills opening up ahead
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba leads a line of Meitei fighters down a forested ridge, the open Manipur valley visible ahead under a clearing sky.

dialogue.speaker: Khuman Ngamba
dialogue.text: Seven years we walked in exile. Today, we walk home.

i18n.hi: सात साल हम जला-वतनी चले। आज, घर की ओर चल रहे हैं।

panels.shot: wide, quiet shot of re-entered Kangla—ruined, overgrown, yet familiar
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba steps slowly through the broken gate of Kangla, touching a cracked wall as weeds and saplings grow between fallen stones.

dialogue.text: By 1826, Burmese forces withdrew under treaty pressures and war. The Meitei returned to a capital scarred and emptied, but still standing by the Imphal river.

i18n.hi: १८२६ तक, संधियों और जंग के दबाव में बर्मी फ़ौजें लौट गईं। मैतेइ इम्फाल नदी किनारे खड़ी, घायल और खाली राजधानी में लौटे।

panels.shot: medium shot of villagers reunited, embracing in the courtyard of a partly rebuilt homestead
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba embraces surviving kin in a courtyard where new bamboo posts rise among old foundations, children watching with wary, hopeful eyes.

dialogue.text: Families stitched themselves together from fragments—those who survived Ava, those who hid in the hills, those who never returned. The kingdom lived, but changed forever.

i18n.hi: परिवार टुकड़ों से खुद को सीने लगे—जो अवा से बचे, जो पहाड़ों में छिपे, और जो कभी लौट न पाए। राज्य जिंदा रहा, पर हमेशा के लिए बदल गया।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of an elder telling the story to children around a hearth, manuscripts beside him
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba, now older, sits by a hearth in Kangla, recounting the Seven Years to a circle of children as palm-leaf manuscripts rest nearby.

dialogue.text: Chronicles recorded Chahi Taret Khuntakpa in spare lines. In homes, elders filled those lines with tears, names and vows that the valley’s silence would never be forgotten.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथों ने चाही तरेत खुंतक्पा को थोड़ी पंक्तियों में बाँधा। घरों में बुज़ुर्गों ने उन पंक्तियों को आँसुओं, नामों और उन क़समों से भरा कि घाटी की खामोशी कभी नहीं भूली जाएगी।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the Manipur valley at sunrise, fields green again but Kangla’s ruins still visible
panels.action: Khuman Ngamba stands on a rise at dawn, overlooking newly green paddy fields and the distant outline of Kangla, hands folded as if in quiet promise.

dialogue.text: The Seven Years Devastation was wrought by kings’ ambitions and armies’ orders, but endured by farmers, soldiers and exiles. Their memory turned a wound into a warning—and a people into survivors.

i18n.hi: सात साल की तबाही राजाओं की चाह और फौजों के हुक्म से आई, पर किसानों, सिपाहियों और जला-वतनी लोगों ने झेली। उनकी याद ने ज़ख्म को चेतावनी बनाया—और एक क़ौम को सिर्फ़ पीड़ित नहीं, बचने वाला बना दिया।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Valley Emptied and Memory Fought On
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब घाटी खाली हुई, पर यादें लड़ती रहीं
